sourceCopy.examplesHeading: Four useful ways to get started

examples.heading: On the birthday itself
examples.text: From 2000-01-15 to 2025-01-15, the age is 25 years, 0 months and 0 days. The birthday countdown is zero.

examples.heading: The day before a birthday
examples.text: From 2000-01-15 to 2025-01-14, the calendar age is 24 years, 11 months and 30 days.

examples.heading: February 28 convention
examples.text: For a 2024-02-29 birth, 2025-02-28 counts as the first birthday when February 28 is selected.

examples.heading: March 1 convention
examples.text: With March 1 selected, the same 2025-02-28 reference is still 0 years, 11 months and 30 days.

steps.heading: Choose the question
steps.text: Select the mode that matches your task. The input labels follow that choice.

steps.heading: Enter the values
steps.text: Age is based on calendar dates, without birth times. Choose the leap-day birthday convention explicitly.

steps.heading: Check the result
steps.text: Calculate, inspect the working and save the result if needed. Cancel stops a long job.

method.heading: The method behind this result
paragraphs: Calendar age counts completed birthday anniversaries, then complete months and remaining days. It is not total days divided by 365. Month lengths and leap years vary, so that division cannot reproduce an exact years-months-days interval.

All entered dates are Gregorian civil dates. They are represented at UTC midnight for arithmetic, so a daylight-saving clock change does not add or remove a calendar day. No birth time or time zone is inferred from the input.

A February 29 birth needs a convention in years without that date. February 28 and March 1 are both offered explicitly. The selected convention affects the anniversary anchor, completed years and the birthday countdown. The page does not choose a legal rule for a jurisdiction.

After the completed years, the calculation advances complete months from the anniversary anchor. A target month that lacks the anchor day uses its final day. The remaining difference is then counted in days. The working shows the month anchor used for that remainder.

Total days is the date difference without adding an extra inclusive day. The next birthday is today when the reference date is an anniversary, giving a zero countdown. Otherwise it is the next anniversary according to the selected leap-day convention.

The initial reference date comes from the device’s local calendar date. You can replace it with a historical or future reference. Dates use the browser’s native supported range; an unavailable later birthday is labelled rather than replaced with a fabricated date.

uses.heading: Use the result with the right assumptions
paragraphs: Use this for a personal date comparison or a planning note where calendar years and remaining months matter. Verify the selected reference date, especially if the device clock is wrong or the page has been open across midnight.

The same date pair can have different year-month-day descriptions under different month-end conventions. Total elapsed calendar days remains a separate, useful check. The chosen method is described so the output is reproducible instead of merely appearing exact.

Legal eligibility, medical ages and jurisdiction-specific birthday rules require their own authoritative interpretation. This page performs calendar arithmetic and displays a convention; it does not establish an official age status.

privacy.heading: Private calculations, clear limits
paragraphs: Your inputs and results stay in this browser. Calculation runs in a local worker, without a calculation API or uploaded data.
The page saves only your theme preference. A copied link contains the selected inputs and options, so share it deliberately.
Large calculations depend on device time and memory. Cancel stops the active job. An error clears old answers and disables their downloads.

faq.question: Does this use my birth time?
faq.answer: No. It compares calendar dates only. Hours, time zones and the exact instant of birth are not part of this model.

faq.question: Why not divide total days by 365?
faq.answer: Years and months have different lengths. Calendar age counts anniversaries and complete months before the remaining days.

faq.question: How are February 29 birthdays treated?
faq.answer: Choose February 28 or March 1 for a non-leap year. The anniversary and countdown use that visible convention.

faq.question: What happens on my birthday?
faq.answer: The completed-year count increases, and the birthday shown for the reference date has a countdown of zero.

faq.question: Are total days inclusive?
faq.answer: No extra inclusive day is added. A birth date equal to the reference date gives zero elapsed days.

faq.question: Can I choose a future reference date?
faq.answer: Yes. Any valid reference on or after the birth date is accepted within the supported calendar range.

faq.question: Where does the default comparison date come from?
faq.answer: The browser reads the device’s local calendar date when the page loads. You can change the field explicitly.

faq.question: Can daylight saving change the total days?
faq.answer: Not here. The arithmetic uses civil dates at UTC midnight, rather than local clock-hour differences.

faq.question: Why can month-end results look unusual?
faq.answer: Missing target days are constrained to the end of the month. The working shows the anchor before the remaining days are counted.

faq.question: Does this determine my legal age?
faq.answer: No. It shows calendar arithmetic with a chosen leap-day convention. Official eligibility rules require the relevant authoritative rule.
